first_impression.reaction: I searched 'getting married in seychelles' because it's on the list next to Mauritius and Italy. The intro answers Dad's first question, whether it's legal, in two lines, with no 'paradise' nonsense, so I kept going. I read the documents, banns and certificate sections properly and the guest-health bits got my attention because of James's grandmother. Where I lost the thread was the beach: I finished the page and still can't tell whether we can legally marry on the sand or have to do it in an office in Victoria. The islands section also doesn't help us choose between them.

journey.quote: The Seychelles is on your shortlist, and before you choose a bay or a resort you want to know one thing: will the marriage stand? It will.
journey.reaction: Straight answer up front, then the process. As a lawyer I like that it says who registers the marriage instead of just promising it's simple.

journey.quote: The Australian High Commission's guidance for couples marrying in the Seychelles is that a church wedding without a civil ceremony is not legally recognised, so the civil marriage comes first.
journey.reaction: Useful for my parents, who'd assume a church service covers it. Citing the High Commission is the kind of source I'd actually trust.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Look at your guests' routes as well as your own, particularly anyone pairing the wedding with time on the African mainland.
journey.reaction: Finally someone thinks about the guests. Half our list is flying from overseas and a few of them would definitely do a safari first. That's an insider detail.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Take out travel insurance that covers medical evacuation, for the two of you and for any parents travelling with you.
journey.reaction: Slightly scary but honest. This is exactly the grandparents question and I'd rather know now. Forwarding this to Mum.

journey.section: What the Civil Status office asks for
journey.quote: One question to settle early: whether the office accepts certified copies of your birth and divorce certificates, or wants the originals.
journey.reaction: Good to flag, but it's the first of a lot of 'ask the office' moments. I start to wonder what the article actually knows versus what it's passing back to us.

journey.section: The banns and a special licence
journey.quote: Arrive early enough for the banns to run and you have days in hand. Arrive closer to the date and the licence is the route, so ask the office what it needs to see with your application.
journey.reaction: Clear trade-off. Eleven days or a licence in about two. I could plan flights around this, which is more than most pages give me.

journey.quote: If you would like your marriage registered at home rather than at the office, tell the Civil Status office at least a week before the wedding takes place.
journey.reaction: 'At home' meaning where? Our home in Sydney? A villa? Later the page has a heading about registering at home in Australia and says you can't. I read this three times and I'm still not sure what it means for a resort ceremony.

journey.section: Who performs the ceremony, and where
journey.quote: Your marriage is registered by the Civil Status office, and a Civil Status Officer travels to you when you marry away from the main islands.
journey.reaction: So the officer travels to outer islands, but on Mahé or Praslin do we go to the office? This contradicts the picture I had of a beach ceremony and the article never squares it.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, at your resort or on another island
journey.quote: People in the Seychelles are usually very traditional, so avoid public displays of affection, especially in rural or traditional places.
journey.reaction: Didn't know this at all. Genuinely useful, and the point about a public beach versus a private terrace is the kind of thing that would save us an awkward moment in front of our friends.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, at your resort or on another island
journey.quote: Step-free access. Can older guests and anyone using a wheelchair reach the ceremony space, the reception and their rooms without steps or sand?
journey.reaction: The resort question list is excellent. I'd copy the whole thing into our planning doc. This one in particular is our grandparents worry, word for word.

journey.section: When to marry in the Seychelles
journey.quote: Smartraveller notes that heavy rain can occur, especially during the monsoon season from November to March, causing flooding and landslides that damage roads.
journey.reaction: Monsoon, dengue, rips. Every line is a warning and none of it tells me which months are actually good. I skimmed the rest and came out knowing when not to go but not when to go.

journey.quote: The island you choose shapes the logistics as much as the view.
journey.reaction: Then it tells me each island has an office and some buses. Nothing on what each feels like, how far from the airport, which suits 80 guests versus 20. This is the actual decision we face and the section doesn't help us make it.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One contact and inclusions in writing is what we want. 'Start to finish' is the line every planner uses though, and there's no Seychelles wedding here to back it.

journey.quote: Ask the office and your resort together whether the beach in front of your resort can host the civil ceremony, and who arranges the officer's attendance.
journey.reaction: I asked 'can we marry on the beach' and got 'ask someone else'. It's the most important question for us and the FAQ doesn't say yes, no or it depends.

journey.section: Plan your Seychelles wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD and the fee in writing hit our currency-surprise fear directly. Calm close, no pressure. Good, but not enough on its own to make me enquire.

unanswered_questions: Can the legal civil ceremony actually happen on a beach or resort lawn on Mahé, Praslin or La Digue, or only in the office?
What does 'registered at home rather than at the office' mean in the Seychelles, and does it cover a resort?
Does the office accept certified copies, or do we have to post or carry our original birth certificates?
Do we need witnesses, and how many?
Which months are best for a wedding with older guests, not just which to avoid?
How do Mahé, Praslin, La Digue and the private islands compare for guest numbers, airport distance and feel?
How much are the government fees for the special licence and the officer's attendance? (fee amounts deferred)
Who is actually on the ground in the Seychelles on the day: your own person or a local partner? (deferred business detail)
Do you have a real Seychelles wedding (venue, island, date) we can look at? (deferred business detail)
How does Wedded Wonderland charge: flat fee, percentage, commissions? Is there a starting range? (deferred business detail)
Will you handle the document pack, the banns or special licence and the Supreme Court apostille, or is that on us? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange guest transfers and inter-island ferries or flights, including for the officer? (deferred business detail)
Are there perks or Wedded Privileges at Seychelles resorts? (deferred business detail)
How many Seychelles weddings have you planned? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask the office and your resort together whether the beach in front of your resort can host the civil ceremony, and who arranges the officer's attendance.
turn_offs_found.why: The headline question in the FAQ gets bounced back to us. It feels like the article doesn't know, and it's the one thing my friends would ask first.

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish
turn_offs_found.why: 'Start to finish' is the generic end-to-end claim every planner makes. Without a Seychelles wedding or a named person on the ground, it reads flatter than the specific advice above it.

would_share_with: James: 'The banns and a special licence' and the resort question list, because they decide when we fly and what we ask venues
My parents: the intro, the 'Civil, religious or symbolic' section and the medical evacuation line, because Dad will ask if it's legal and Mum will worry about Nan

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-seychelles&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: No pressure, and AUD plus fee in writing are the right reassurances. But we're 14 months out, the Seychelles is one of a few options, the beach question isn't answered and I haven't seen a real Seychelles wedding from them. I'd read the Mauritius guide first and come back.

top_3_changes: Answer the beach question plainly: say where the civil ceremony can legally take place on the main islands and what 'registered at home' means, because 'If you would like your marriage registered at home rather than at the office' and the beach FAQ leave us unsure whether the sand is possible at all.

Make 'Choosing your island' compare the islands for a couple with guests (feel, guest numbers, airport and transfer time, ease for older relatives), since 'The island you choose shapes the logistics as much as the view.' sets up a comparison the section never delivers.

Give 'When to marry' at least one positive steer on which months suit a wedding, and rename the 'Recognition and registering at home' heading so it doesn't clash with the Seychelles 'registered at home' option.
